metaData.originalTitle: 浙大×阿里云首发 Token 经济学综述：重估 LLM Agent 的 Token 世界
metaData.title: Zhejiang University × Alibaba Cloud Release First Token Economics Survey: Re-evaluating the Token World of LLM Agents
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Zhejiang University and Alibaba Cloud jointly released a Token Economics survey, systematically reviewing LLM Agent token consumption, cost optimization, collaboration, and security governance from both computing and economics perspectives.
metaData.summary: This article is an interpretation of the survey paper "Token Economics for LLM Agents: A Dual-View Study from Computing and Economics" jointly released by Zhejiang University and Alibaba Cloud. The paper points out that as LLM Agents move into high-stakes scenarios such as finance, law, and healthcare, tokens have evolved from a technical unit into a core resource affecting system cost, latency, security, and scalability. The paper proposes a Dual-View framework that links computer science Agent optimization problems with economic theories (factors of production, medium of exchange, unit of account) and constructs a four-dimensional classification system: single-agent token efficiency (trade-offs between reasoning and tool invocation), multi-agent collaboration costs (communication and division of labor friction), Agent ecosystem pricing and governance (platform economy and Jevons paradox), and the security dimension (equilibrium between defense expenditure and attack losses). The paper also outlines six major trends and five emerging opportunities, including differentiable token budgets, real-time token markets, and agent-level token scaling laws.

mainPoints.point: Tokens are endowed with three economic attributes: factors of production, medium of exchange, and unit of account.
mainPoints.explanation: Generating tokens consumes computational capital, billing by token makes them a pricing unit, and task complexity can be quantified through token expenditure, providing a unified analytical language for Agent system optimization.

mainPoints.point: Single agents must find the optimal cost substitution between internal reasoning tokens and external tool invocation tokens.
mainPoints.explanation: The cost structures of internal tokens (e.g., chain-of-thought, planning) and external tokens (e.g., retrieval, API calls) differ; systems need to weigh the marginal cost of "letting the model think more" versus "calling external tools."

mainPoints.point: In multi-agent systems, communication costs may grow superlinearly, offsetting the benefits of specialized division of labor.
mainPoints.explanation: An increase in the number of agents brings communication tokens, coordination costs, and scheduling friction. The key challenge is finding the optimal balance between specialization gains and collaboration friction, rather than simply having more agents.

mainPoints.point: Lower inference costs may stimulate demand, leading to an increase in total token consumption (Jevons paradox).
mainPoints.explanation: At the macro level, cost reduction does not necessarily decrease total consumption; instead, it may cause usage to continue growing due to demand elasticity, posing new challenges for platform pricing and resource governance.

mainPoints.point: Security should be treated as an endogenous constraint of the token economy, not an external add-on module.
mainPoints.explanation: The paper constructs a cost model under security constraints, revealing the trade-off between defense expenditure and expected attack losses. The optimal security investment depends on the equilibrium between the two.

keyQuotes: Tokens are no longer just a technical unit in model input and output; they are becoming a core resource affecting system cost, latency, security, and scalability.

Lower inference costs do not necessarily mean lower total consumption. On the contrary, cost reductions may stimulate more demand, leading to a continued rise in overall token usage. This resembles the Jevons-like dynamics in economics.
Security should not be viewed as an external compliance module attached to Agent systems, but should be incorporated as an endogenous constraint of Token Economics.

relatedArticles.title: Fearless of Off-Policy Shift! Bengio Team Decouples Post-Training, Accelerating LLM RL by 50x
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Bengio team proposes the TBA asynchronous framework, which decouples sampling from training and introduces a trajectory balance objective, accelerating LLM RL post-training by up to 50x while maintaining or improving performance.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: From P(y|x) to P(y): Bringing RL into the Pretraining Space to Unlock the Intrinsic Reasoning of Large Models
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Institutions including the Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences propose PreRL and DSRL methods, which directly optimize the marginal distribution P(y) of reasoning trajectories instead of the conditional distribution P(y|x), combined with negative sample reinforcement. In just 20 steps, they significantly unlock the intrinsic reasoning capabilities of large models, surpassing existing strong baselines on multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.

relatedArticles.title: Attention Is All You Need Authors Strike Again: Can a 99% Sparse Transformer Be Faster?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A new study co-authored by the original authors of "Attention Is All You Need" uses L1 regularization to induce FFN activation sparsity, combined with the TwELL sparse format and custom CUDA kernels, to translate 99% sparsity into real inference and training speedups.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: The First Survey on Agent Harness: Beyond the Model, What Makes an Agent?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article reviews the concept of Agent Harness Engineering proposed by institutions including CMU, Yale, and Amazon, integrating execution environment, tool interface, context management, lifecycle orchestration, observability, validation and evaluation, and governance and security into the ETCLOVG seven-layer architecture, demonstrating the decisive impact of systems engineering beyond the model on Agent reliability.

relatedArticles.title: CVPR 2026 | Rotating the Semantic Rubik's Cube: SafeRoPE Ensures Safety in Next-Generation Text-to-Image Generation
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: The Fudan JADE team proposes SafeRoPE, a technique that leverages risk-aware rotary position encoding to directionally regulate risk semantics within the semantic space of MMDiT-based text-to-image models, achieving synergistic optimization of safety and generation quality.
